stories.headline: Spain votes in snap election
stories.summary: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez held a final rally urging supporters to turn out, hoping to defy the polls, while his main rivals accused him of not telling the truth and of "betrayal". The election could end his eight years in power, according to CNBC. The Financial Times describes his tenure as possibly ending over anger about migration and housing.

stories.headline: Quebec religious symbols ban largely upheld
stories.summary: Canada's top court largely upheld Quebec's law barring public servants from wearing religious symbols. The law was challenged by groups including female Muslim, Sikh and Catholic teachers, who argued it violated their fundamental rights. The Guardian describes the ruling as exposing tensions between minority rights and government power.

stories.headline: Peru helicopter crash kills eight
stories.summary: Eight people died when a Peruvian military helicopter crashed during a rescue mission in a remote area known for drug trafficking. The pilot was the sole survivor.

stories.headline: Kenyan cult leader convicted of further killings
stories.summary: Paul Mackenzie was found guilty of killing 123 more followers, weeks after being jailed for the mass murder of children. The convictions relate to his doomsday cult.

stories.headline: Zelensky criticises Trump-Putin relationship
stories.summary: Ukraine's president described the Trump-Putin friendship as "strange" in a BBC interview. He said the US is not pushing Russia hard enough in peace talks to end the war.

stories.headline: Taiwan holds local elections
stories.summary: Taiwanese voters went to the polls in local elections seen as a test for the ruling Democratic Progressive Party. Key mayoral race in Taipei, a stronghold of the opposition Kuomintang, is closely watched. Officials have raised alarm over Chinese interference.

stories.headline: Israeli strike hits MSF Gaza clinic
stories.summary: An Israeli strike on a Doctors Without Borders clinic in Gaza killed two staff, described by MSF as a 'direct hit'. MSF has called for those responsible to be held accountable.

stories.headline: Norse Atlantic Airways goes bankrupt
stories.summary: Norwegian budget airline Norse Atlantic filed for bankruptcy and cancelled all future flights after failing to secure funding. Soaring fuel costs linked to the Iran war strained its finances. It told customers not to come to airports.

stories.headline: Chinese stocks post biggest one-day gains
stories.summary: Chinese chip stocks had their biggest ever one-day gains after a rare midday state media statement pledged market liquidity support. Bloomberg reports the rally was the biggest stock gain since 2024.

stories.headline: Poundland enters administration
stories.summary: Poundland has gone into administration, leaving staff fearful about Christmas and facing closures and job losses. The Guardian reports 2,000 suppliers will take a big hit.

stories.headline: S&P cuts France outlook and Wall Street correction
stories.summary: S&P cut France's outlook to negative, citing political instability that will make it harder to tackle the public deficit. Separately, CNBC reports the S&P 500 has entered a correction after a November sell-off, though corrections do not always lead to bear markets.

stories.headline: Dangote Refinery plans blockbuster IPO
stories.summary: Africa's richest man is taking his Dangote Refinery public, with an IPO that could value the company at about $47 billion. It is expected to be Africa's biggest stock market listing.

stories.headline: Banks may pass on £1.5bn tax rise
stories.summary: Bank of England governor Andrew Bailey warned banks could try to pass on the £1.5bn cost of a temporary corporation tax surcharge to customers. He said lenders will aim to protect their earnings.

stories.headline: Forest beat Chelsea 3-2
stories.summary: Morgan Gibbs-White scored twice as Nottingham Forest beat Chelsea 3-2, their first win over them at the City Ground since 1997. Igor Jesus also scored a stunning volley. Chelsea lost their third Premier League game in a row, and Wesley Fofana was booed by his own fans after a controversial interview.

stories.headline: England beat Australia in third T20
stories.summary: England beat Australia by seven wickets in the third T20 at The Gabba, taking the series lead. Overton took five wickets in a fiery spell that helped England flip the Gabba script.

stories.headline: Ireland beat Australia 38-14 in rugby
stories.summary: Ireland beat Australia 38-14 in London, with five tries, to finish fifth in the inaugural Nations Championship. McNabney scored a late double.

stories.headline: Aston Villa: Emery on Garnacho
stories.summary: Aston Villa boss Unai Emery praised Alejandro Garnacho's "fantastic attitude" but suggested other players rank ahead of him for selection.

stories.headline: Lyon left out of Australia squad
stories.summary: Australia have dropped off-spinner Nathan Lyon for the first Test against New Zealand in Perth, starting 9 December. Australia's chair of selectors said he expects Lyon to tour India, but Lyon is considering his future.

stories.headline: Rodgers texts into broadcast after Steelers win
stories.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers beat Denver Broncos 27-5. Aaron Rodgers was released after a rift with head coach Mike McCarthy and texted into an Amazon broadcast to defend himself.

stories.headline: Thanksgiving storms leave hundreds of thousands without power
stories.summary: Severe weather on both US coasts during Thanksgiving left hundreds of thousands without power, with the Macy's parade postponed. Trees fell and roads flooded, and the clean-up continues.

stories.headline: African megacities sinking faster than thought
stories.summary: New satellite data shows cities including Lagos and Alexandria are sinking faster than previously thought. A study says sinking land and rising seas could expose more than seven million people in Africa's coastal megacities to flooding by 2050.

stories.headline: CF Industries to buy Mosaic ammonia complex
stories.summary: CF Industries agreed to acquire Mosaic's Faustina ammonia complex in a $600m deal.

stories.headline: Depardieu ordered to stand trial
stories.summary: French actor Gérard Depardieu has been ordered to stand trial for rape and sexual assault. The case is one of the most prominent in France's reckoning with sexual violence.

stories.headline: Channel 4 defends Huw Edwards documentary
stories.summary: Channel 4 defended its decision to make a documentary about disgraced former BBC newsreader Huw Edwards, saying it "holds him to account, with no questions off limits". Downing Street said it has no interest in hearing from him.

stories.headline: Phoebe Bridgers phone-free tour review
stories.summary: A Guardian review praised Phoebe Bridgers' phone-free arena show at Co-op Live in Manchester as a cosmic, communal experience. Bridgers banned phones on her Lost Weekend tour.

stories.headline: Mike Leigh announces final film
stories.summary: Director Mike Leigh has announced that Tender Loving Care will be his last film, after 55 years of work.

stories.headline: Floating islands for Glasgow parks
stories.summary: Floating nature islands are being planted in five Glasgow parks as a Games legacy. They are designed to encourage wildlife and help clean the water.

stories.headline: Rare turtles rescued from airport baggage
stories.summary: Endangered turtles were found in baggage at Amsterdam airport. Officials say they had been bound with duct tape.

stories.headline: Mad about mara: Nigerian DIY dance movement
stories.summary: A DIY dance movement called mara has grown from one artist's response to being cut out of a music video into a driving force in Nigeria's cultural landscape, helping young people escape the daily grind.

stories.headline: Mathematics and AI
stories.summary: AI has helped crack a problem that has defied mathematicians since 1859, the Riemann hypothesis, prompting a Guardian editorial on whether its power will stay in the hands of billionaires.
